name: Helms Row
description: The Helms Row is performed with the chest supported on an incline bench set to 30-45 degrees, with a dumbbell in each hand hanging freely. The chest support eliminates lower back and hip contribution, allowing the back muscles to work in complete isolation. The incline angle also allows greater shoulder extension ROM compared to a flat bench row, increasing lat engagement at the bottom of each repetition.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to 30-45 degrees of incline. Lie prone (chest-down) with the chest on the pad, feet on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust bench angle so the arms can fully extend downward without hitting the floor. Use a bench height that allows free arm movement.
steps: Step 1: Lie on the incline bench with chest fully supported, dumbbells hanging.
Step 2: Retract the scapulae slightly to begin the movement.
Step 3: Row both dumbbells toward the lower ribcage, driving the elbows upward and back.
Step 4: At the top, squeeze the rhomboids and mid-traps hard.
Step 5: Lower both dumbbells fully under control to the extended starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad, reintroducing lower back and hip involvement
Using too heavy a weight, causing the elbows to flare excessively
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
safety_considerations: Keep the chest on the pad throughout — that is the defining feature of this exercise
Neck should remain in neutral — do not crane the head up
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom to elbows above the torso level at the top.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top
Let the dumbbells hang fully at the bottom
